OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `PowerModel.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal` EXISTS in the sim now. `Power.should_owner_death_trigger_fatal` defaults to True (PowerModel.cs:646) and the two non-mock overrides are ported at their own sites -- MinionPower unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and ReattachPower as `_all_others_down()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109, whose own comment says "shouldn't trigger fatal unless all other segments are dead too"). `cmds.should_trigger_fatal(target)` is the `Target.Powers.All(...)` test, and BOTH Fatal cards call it BEFORE their attack, which is where C# reads it and is load-bearing: the killing blow strips the very powers the test asks about (Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath). This is NOT death prevention -- the minion really dies -- which is exactly why the `is_dead` check both cards already had did not cover it. EXECUTED: Hand of Greed into a minion at 1 HP kills it and grants 0 gold where it used to grant 20.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  Same mechanism and same fix as card/feed (rule 3) -- these are the pool's only two Fatal cards. NOT CLOSED: the gold still reaches the run through `combat.gold_gained` at finish_combat rather than PlayerCmd.GainGold immediately, which this entry already recorded as a same-end-state re-architecture.  The text it replaced read: The damage and the gold amount are faithful, and the gold does reach the run (`ctx.combat.gold_gained += self._gold`, credited by finish_combat) where C# calls `PlayerCmd.GainGold` immediately -- a timing re-architecture with the same end state. THE FATAL TEST DROPS ITS POWER-VETO HALF, exactly as card/feed's does. C# computes `bool shouldTriggerFatal = cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` BEFORE the attack (HandOfGreed.cs:49) and requires it alongside `WasTargetKilled` (58); the sim tests only `was_alive and target.is_dead` (colorless_attacks.py:200-202). The sim's docstring asserts "no implemented power vetoes fatal" -- THAT IS FALSE. Two C# powers do: `MinionPower` unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and `ReattachPower` unless every other segment is dead (ReattachPower.cs:106-109), and BOTH are ported -- MinionPower at powers.py:1536-1542, applied by three ported monsters (`monsters/glory/fabricator.py:182`, `monsters/glory/queen.py:50`, `monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:128`), ReattachPower at powers.py:2360. Kill a Fabricator bot, a Queen minion or an Ovicopter egg with Hand of Greed: the game grants no gold, the sim grants 20. LIVE, and the same mechanism and verdict as card/feed's OnPlay entry (rule 3) -- these are the only two Fatal cards in the pool and both have it. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): MinionPower.cs, ReattachPower.cs, powers.py and the three monster modules are not hashed.
